## Highlights

- **`tale deploy prepare` fetches a configuration source from Forgejo over HTTPS.** A managed deployment's `configs[].repository` can now name a configuration repository on an allowed Forgejo host (today `git.tale.dev` only) as well as on GitHub. Preparation fetches it over HTTPS with a read-only access token from the new `TALE_SOURCE_TOKEN`. The CLI hands the token to Git through its environment configuration for that host alone, on the fetch step only, never in arguments, the remote URL, a file or a log, and keeps it out of the bundle and the runtime. Every source is checked before any Git step: an off-list host, a URL that is not canonical (a port, credentials, `.git`, a query or a trailing slash) and a Forgejo source without a token are refused, and a refused token gets the hint `authentication` ([Prepare, verify, and apply the bundle](https://docs.tale.dev/self-hosted/install/cli-install#prepare-verify-and-apply-the-bundle), [#5514](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/5514)).
- **A sandbox device can run its sessions directly on its machine.** `tale sandbox connect … --runtime raw` connects a device whose sessions run with no container and no virtual machine, on the harnesses installed on that machine (Claude Code, Codex, …). Connected as root, each session runs as its own slot account, and stop and destroy end every process of the slot and take back its temporary files; connected as an ordinary account, sessions share it, for a machine its owner uses alone. The release's `tale` binary carries the device's runtime, so a raw device needs no Docker, and its update refuses a binary whose checksum is not the release's. The device list shows where a device runs its sandboxes and which harnesses it holds. Docker devices and the server's sandboxes run as before ([Run sandboxes directly on the machine](https://docs.tale.dev/platform/admin/sandbox-devices#raw-devices), [#5512](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/5512)).
- **Tasks and automations can run on a device's own Claude Code sign-in.** `tale sandbox login claude-code` stores the token `claude setup-token` prints on the device, and the new Anthropic credential method **Sign-in on a sandbox device** runs tasks and automations on it, never chat. The token never leaves the device. When a sign-in reaches its usage limit, the run moves to another connected device whose sign-in is free, or waits as **Waiting for a sign-in to reset** until the earliest reset; Claude Code's and Codex's usage limits now end a turn as a usage limit instead of a failure ([Use the device's own subscription](https://docs.tale.dev/platform/admin/sandbox-devices#sign-ins), [#5513](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/5513)).
- **A chat's code step waits its turn on a busy sandbox host.** `run_code` failed with **The sandbox host is busy** the moment the sandbox host refused a light sandbox, and gave up its place in the host's line. It now waits at the host's hint for up to a minute in a chat and up to about 90 seconds in a task run, keeps its place, and the platform logs what the host was short of when it started or gave up ([#5510](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/5510)).
- **Agent runtimes ignore a workspace's own agent configuration.** Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Gemini CLI and Qwen Code now run on the configuration Tale gives them, not on files such as `.claude/settings.json`, `.codex/config.toml` or `opencode.json` that a repository carries for its own use. The repository's `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `GEMINI.md` and `QWEN.md` and its skills still guide the agent ([#5500](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/5500)).
- **A video's captions are taken when its page offers no format.** A caption download failed with "Requested format is not available" when YouTube offered the caller's address no format but served the captions; the transcript is now written ([#5509](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/5509)).

## Upgrade notes

- **Platform:** run the `0.5.109` images and upgrade the `tale` CLI with them. This release does not change the API contract version. It adds two database migrations, both safe during a rolling deploy: `0239_device_login_credentials.sql` lets a provider credential use the method `device-login`, and `0240_usage_limit_holds.sql` adds the table `app.usage_limit_holds` and the waiting reasons `usage_limit` and `device_login` for parked runs. No configuration change is needed.
- **A workspace with its own `.gemini/.env` or `.qwen/settings.json`:** Gemini CLI and Qwen Code no longer start there; the run fails at once, and its reason names the file. Remove the file from the repository, or run the task on another runtime.
- **Forgejo configuration sources are opt-in.** A deployment whose configuration sources are on GitHub prepares as before. To move one to `git.tale.dev`, point its `configs[].repository` at the canonical `https://git.tale.dev/<owner>/<repo>` and give `tale deploy prepare` a read-only `TALE_SOURCE_TOKEN`; a release descriptor in that repository must name the same address.
- **Raw devices and device sign-ins are opt-in.** Devices connected without `--runtime raw`, and credentials of the existing methods, behave as before. A raw device's sandboxes use the machine's own network, with no egress proxy: fence the machine before you connect it.
